text.arabic_uthmani: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

words.gloss_range: sequential-consequential connector fused to the following action; not an independent lexical noun or verb
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) makes the rescue report start as consequence rather than as a new scene. It ties 51:35 to the marked punishment of 51:34, so the removal of the believers reads as the next movement inside one judgment-and-rescue operation. Its fused placement on the following verb also lets the boundary hinge and the extraction arrive as one surface action, with the abrupt onset giving the pivot audible force.

topics.headline: immediate consequence across the ayah boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that rescue is not detached from judgment; it follows the prior threat as its immediate protective counterpart.
topics.reason: The particle is a conjunction marking sequential action, and the preceding ayah supplies the threat that this ayah answers.

topics.headline: fused connector launches the action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the boundary marker is attached to the rescue verb, making transition and act arrive together.
topics.reason: The written form attaches the connector to the verb, while the sound row supports an abrupt audible entry into the action.

words.gloss_range: completed active causative extraction of persons to safety in this clause; not passive departure or a generic production sense
words.root_gloss_range: broad field of going out, bringing out, yield, emergence, and departure; this Form IV verb selects causative bringing-out while some yield and emergence imagery remains only as controlled resonance
words.prose: {{ar:أَخْرَجْنَا}} ({{tr:akhrajnā}}) is the governing rescue verb: a completed active Form IV act in which the divine speaker causes the qualifying people to be brought out. The object, location, and final category make the verb a selection funnel rather than a loose motion verb. Through {{ar:خ ر ج}} ({{tr:kh-r-j}}), the movement is spatially exact: people who had been inside are made to cross out from the threatened place. The yield and fruit-extraction echoes remain secondary but visible, casting the believers as the valuable human output separated from ruin, while cross-passage contrasts show the same outward motion can be rescue here, expulsion in Adam scenes (7:27; 20:123), or another divine handling of enemies in the same surah (51:40).

topics.headline: completed divine causative extraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescued group as acted upon by divine agency, not as self-evacuating or awaiting rescue.
topics.reason: The QAC analysis gives a perfect active first plural Form IV verb, and attachment evidence gives an explicit object governed by the verb.

topics.headline: main verb controls the filtering syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the sentence as a narrowing process: action, then qualifying object, then location and class.
topics.reason: The verb governs the relative object, while the later locative and category phrases define the extracted set.

topics.headline: inside-to-outside rescue motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete boundary crossing: those who were inside the threatened place are made to emerge from it.
topics.reason: The locally selected branch is causative bringing-out, supported by the following locative clause that supplies the interior.

topics.headline: valuable output and emergence imagery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a controlled bringing-forth resonance: the saved people are drawn out like valuable output, while the local sense remains rescue-extraction.
topics.reason: V4 lists yield and emergence as accepted root branches, but the local Form IV human object selects rescue, so the imagery is resonance rather than the primary lexical sense.

topics.headline: same outward motion, opposite outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that outward movement is morally determined by object and context: here it saves believers, elsewhere it can expel or seize.
topics.reason: Rows cite Adam-expulsion references (7:27; 20:123), the believer pattern in 2:257, and the same-surah contrast at 51:40.

topics.headline: abrupt intervention at the scene cut
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the transition as an intervention: the stored threat turns into executed rescue before destruction proceeds.
topics.reason: The phonetic and boundary rows converge on the verb as the moment where the prior designation becomes historical action.

words.gloss_range: relative human pronoun functioning as the direct object and opening a qualifying clause; conditional generality is a secondary pressure, not the local parse
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) keeps the extracted object compressed: formally singular, human, and able to gather a plural group without naming individuals. As the direct object of the rescue verb, it forces the reader into the relative clause before the object is fully known. The conditional-like generality is real but narrowed by local syntax: the word functions here as a relative object, while still making the rescue principle sound like whoever met the location and belief conditions was included. Its same-surah recurrence at 51:9 keeps it recognizable as a selection word, and its m/n sound anticipates the final category phrase.

topics.headline: compact human object without names
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the saved are gathered by a qualifying pronoun rather than listed as named individuals.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun the direct object, and the following clause completes who the object is.

topics.headline: relative object with conditional-like generality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears both local identification and principled eligibility: whoever fit the stated conditions belongs in the rescued set.
topics.reason: The surface can support conditional pressure, but the syntactically forced local role is relative pronoun and direct object.

topics.headline: object position becomes eligibility testing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader cannot close the object at once; the word opens a test of where the people were and what class they belonged to.
topics.reason: The pronoun connects the main verb to the relative clause, and the bundle warns that target languages may need to preserve this compressed construction.

topics.headline: selection device recurs and is sounded forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pronoun as a local selection device whose nasal sound is picked up by the final category phrase.
topics.reason: Rows connect this pronoun with a same-surah selection use at 51:9 and with the nasal frame that closes in the final phrase.

words.gloss_range: past copular/deficient verb marking prior locative presence with a following locative predicate; not coming-into-being or making-be
words.root_gloss_range: broad being, occurrence, place, and derived-state field; the local construction selects prior being-in-place while place-family pressure remains relevant
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) makes the middle of the ayah a prior-state checkpoint. The rescued object is not just whoever will be moved, but whoever had already been in the threatened place before extraction. Its masculine singular agreement stays with the compact pronoun rather than the feminine location suffix, so the relative-clause chain remains intact. The broader {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) field is narrowed here to locative existence: not a creative command or making-be, but being found inside a bounded place. That same presence logic echoes the Lot-scene formula at 29:32, now recast from named presence to category-qualified rescue.

topics.headline: prior being-in-place before extraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that rescue answers an already true condition: the group had been inside before they were brought out.
topics.reason: The perfect copular verb takes a locative predicate, making prior presence the selected local force.

topics.headline: singular agreement preserves the pronoun chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that grammar keeps the compact human pronoun as subject even though the final identity will be plural.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the pronoun as the subject of the copular clause, while the verb agrees in masculine singular.

topics.headline: being-root narrowed to locative existence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the place-pressure of the being-root without turning the clause into creation or formation language.
topics.reason: V4 permits broader being and place branches, but the local Form I copular construction with a locative predicate blocks making-be as the selected sense.

topics.headline: Lot-scene presence formula recast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the familiar Lot-scene presence formula return, but with named presence recast as whoever qualified for rescue.
topics.reason: The rows cite the presence-in-the-city formula at 29:32 and show this ayah reshaping it through the pronoun and prior-state verb.

topics.headline: being inside makes bringing-out meaningful
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees belief, being, and extraction linked: the group was already in the relevant state and place before rescue.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles show the relevant roots in ordinary predicational and extraction frames, and the local syntax realizes the relation directly.

words.gloss_range: fused locative preposition plus feminine singular suffix pointing to an implied settlement; marks containment and completes the prior-state predicate
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) supplies the unnamed inside. Its feminine suffix makes the reader recover the settlement from context, while the preposition marks containment rather than source-from movement. That matters because the rescue verb can reverse only a location already established as interior. As the predicate of the prior-state verb, the word closes the location condition before the final identity phrase, so place and class remain two separate filters. The same locative pointer also keeps contact with the Lot-scene presence formula at 29:32 and prepares the next ayah's inventory of what remained in that place.

topics.headline: feminine suffix carries the unnamed settlement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader supplies the threatened settlement even though it is not named in this ayah.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the suffix as a feminine locative pronoun with a discourse-inferred destroyed-settlement antecedent.

topics.headline: containment completes the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the location as an interior condition that the extraction will reverse.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is the predicate of the copular clause and supplies the bounded inside.

topics.headline: location delays final classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader dwells on being inside before the sentence discloses the believer category.
topics.reason: The locative phrase sits between the object pronoun and final class phrase, and the cadence rows mark that middle beat.

topics.headline: presence pointer links backward and forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes one place carrying through the Lot scene: presence inside it precedes rescue and the next ayah reports what remains there.
topics.reason: The rows cite the Lot-scene pointer at 29:32 and the continuation of the same location reference into 51:36-37.

words.gloss_range: preposition introducing the final believer category, validly read with partitive and explicative pressure while governing the following genitive plural
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) opens the final classification beat. It can be heard with partitive force, drawing the rescued from among the believer category, and with explicative force, naming who the qualifying pronoun refers to; local syntax keeps both as controlled selection routes rather than forcing one exclusive paraphrase. The particle also governs the final noun's genitive plural form, making the category grammatically dependent on this small pivot, and its m/n echo helps the particle and category sound like one bound unit. After action and location, it supplies the criterion: not every inhabitant, but the class marked by belief, in contrast with the transgressor category of 51:34.

topics.headline: partitive and explicative selection remain controlled
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final phrase both selecting from and clarifying the rescued group, while keeping rescue tied to belief.
topics.reason: The rows preserve both partitive and bayān readings; attachment evidence strongly licenses the prepositional phrase as specifying the group denoted by the pronoun.

topics.headline: preposition binds the final noun grammatically and sonically
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final category as dependent on the particle, not as a loose apposition or new clause.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following genitive plural noun, and the sound row aligns the phonetic binding with the syntactic dependency.

topics.headline: third filter in the action-location-class sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sentence narrow in three stages, with this particle turning from location to identity.
topics.reason: The particle follows the location clause and introduces the final class, matching the action-location-category funnel described in the rows.

topics.headline: classification turns from punishment target to rescued class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees belief functioning as the criterion for removal, set against the transgressor classification in 51:34.
topics.reason: The rows show the preposition restricting the rescued class and shifting classification from the previous ayah's punished group to this ayah's extracted group.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural Form IV active participle naming the recognized believer class as the final rescued identity
words.root_gloss_range: belief, trust, and security field; local form selects believing/trusting persons while security-granting and divine-title associations remain controlled resonance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ}} ({{tr:al-muʾminīna}}) is the ayah's identity seal. Governed by the preceding preposition, definite, plural, and participial, it names the extracted people as an already recognized class rather than as unnamed survivors. The {{ar:أ م ن}} ({{tr:ʾ-m-n}}) field gives the label more than bare assent: belief, trust, and safety answer the danger of the preceding punishment scene, while the active participle presents that identity as settled at the moment of extraction. The divine-title echo at 59:23 and the human participle are not collapsed, but the security field remains audible. The final word also closes the action-location-class sequence, answers refusal in the Lot-passage contrast (26:111), links to the same-surah reminder group (51:55), and stands between the transgressor category of 51:34 and the submitter category of 51:36. Its nasal binding and repeated -in-style ending cadence make those neighboring category labels audible as a connected chain across 51:34-36.

topics.headline: definite governed believer class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescued people as a known, grammatically governed class, not a vague quality or new subject.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, masculine plural genitive after the preposition, and attachment evidence makes it specify the group denoted by the pronoun.

topics.headline: belief, trust, and security in participial identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the saved class as trusting and security-associated persons inside danger, while the local label remains human believers.
topics.reason: No V4 guardrail exists for this root, so the CRITICAL trust and safety pressure survives, but local morphology and referent profiles keep the sense on human believers.

topics.headline: human participle near the divine security title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a security-field resonance with the divine title at 59:23 without equating human believers with the divine name.
topics.reason: The rows cite the divine title at 59:23; local plural human morphology narrows the echo to resonance rather than identity.

topics.headline: final word seals the action-location-class sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah land not on motion or place, but on the rescued group's identity as the final filter.
topics.reason: The noun completes the third beat after action and location, and its morphology, governance, sound, and boundary contrast converge in the final position.

topics.headline: belief class contrasts refusal and neighboring categories
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the believer label positioned in a chain of categories: refusal in 26:111, transgression in 51:34, reminder-believers in 51:55, and submitters in 51:36.
topics.reason: The rows supply the concrete Lot-passage contrast at 26:111, same-surah recurrence at 51:55, and category boundaries at 51:34 and 51:36.

topics.headline: nasal and ending cadence bind the category phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final category as part of a bound sequence of neighboring plural category endings.
topics.reason: The sound rows identify the nasal binding with the preceding particle and the repeated ending cadence across 51:34-36.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative أخرجنا, the interior deixis فيها, and المؤمنين bind outward movement to an interior group characterized by ء م ن.
baseline_models.mechanism: Causative خروج carries those actually present inside across a boundary, while the security-and-trust branch of ء م ن makes that transfer protective rather than merely expulsive.

activation_trace.role: Passage to an exterior supplies the spatial transfer and makes causative extraction the core operation.
Actual occurrence and presence in time establish that the protected group was situated within the interior when removal occurred.
Settled security and trust supply the group's protected quality and turn outward transfer into deliverance.

changed_reading.before: A group is removed from a place.
changed_reading.after: Those securely present inside are caused to cross outward as a protected group.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أخرجنا and the partitive من المؤمنين permit the embedded believing subset to be both removed and made manifest.
baseline_models.mechanism: The disclosure branch of خ ر ج overlays spatial exit: extraction reveals which occupants carried settled assent, converting evacuation into visible differentiation.

activation_trace.role: Bringing something out of concealment supplies disclosure and makes the extraction expose a previously embedded subset.
Place and station derived from being supply the embedded location from which the subset becomes distinct.
Heart-settling assent supplies the criterion disclosed by the separation rather than treating المؤمنين as an unexplained label.

changed_reading.after: Evacuation simultaneously exposes a believing subset whose settled assent had been embedded among the occupants.

context_deltas.mechanism: The guests' entry and doubled peace establish an inward, secured threshold crossing; the focus reverses the vector by causing the secure occupants to cross outward.

activation_trace.role: Literal entry into an interior supplies the inward vector whose reversal organizes the focus extraction.
Repeated freedom from harm colors the threshold encounter with safety and prepares the protective force of the later exit.
Movement to the outside supplies the inverse threshold vector and completes the in-to-out choreography.
Security and trust identify the outward-moving group as protected rather than rejected.

structural_cues: The ordered window places دخلوا and doubled سلام before أخرجنا, creating a marked inward/outward and safety frame.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: entry, doubled peace, and later causative exit. Reader arrow: the inward visitors initiate a controlled threshold reversal that enables safe outward transfer. Alternative: the entry and greeting may only stage the encounter without defining the extraction.

changed_reading.after: Their extraction is the outward half of a threshold choreography: strangers enter under peace, then the secure occupants are escorted out.

context_deltas.mechanism: An inwardly lodged fear is answered by prohibition of fear and good news; the focus then gives the security branch of المؤمنين a material form by moving its bearers beyond danger.

activation_trace.role: Fear falling secretly into the self supplies the interior affective threat against which enacted security becomes legible.
Dread of an expected harm names both the fear and its verbal cancellation, creating the transition toward safety.
News that opens the face with joy supplies the positive turn from concealed fear to assured futurity.
Security and trust become an operative condition whose bearers receive concrete protection.
Crossing outside materializes the promised safety as relocation beyond the threatened interior.

structural_cues: 51:28 moves from inward fear to لا تخف and بشروه; 51:35 moves those named by ء م ن out of the endangered interior.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: concealed fear, its verbal negation, good news, and later extraction of المؤمنين. Reader arrow: the extraction is the concrete performance of security rather than only transport. Alternative: ء م ن may function only as a group label, and the earlier fear belongs to a different participant.

changed_reading.before: Believers names the identity of those removed.
changed_reading.after: Belief's security dimension is enacted: the identity named by ء م ن becomes an experienced passage beyond expected harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: A dispatched mission names a culpable collective and marked material for limit-crossers; extraction discloses and removes the complementary class before target-specific judgment.

activation_trace.role: Dispatch and setting in motion supply the commissioned procedure within which extraction becomes an ordered operation.
Culpability and offense supply the explicitly named target class against which the extracted class is differentiated.
A visible identifying mark supplies target specificity and turns the intervention into discrimination rather than indiscriminate impact.
Crossing a limit supplies the criterion attached to the marked target and sharpens the boundary between classes.
Bringing a hidden thing into view makes extraction the disclosure of the complementary non-target class.
Settled assent supplies the positive classification exposed and removed before the marked judgment proceeds.

structural_cues: The mission names criminals, specifies marked material for limit-crossers, and then selects من كان فيها من المؤمنين before the aftermath is counted.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: a dispatched mission, a culpable target, marked material, limit-crossers, and extraction. Reader arrow: extraction is the complementary sorting step that clears the non-target class. Alternative: the marking may qualify only the material, while the rescue remains procedurally independent.

changed_reading.before: Believers happen to be spared from a general catastrophe.
changed_reading.after: Extraction is a target-discrimination operation: it reveals and removes the non-target class before a marked judgment reaches its specified class.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate finding reduces the plural المؤمنين to a single household-scale enclave; extraction detaches that social unit from its surrounding place without dissolving its internal belonging.

activation_trace.role: Finding and striking upon something supply the post-extraction audit that determines the group's actual granularity.
Exception and exclusion narrow the result to a sole surviving social unit.
The members of a house supply a corporate household reading rather than counting only a physical building.
Wholeness and freedom from harm reinforce the household as the intact unit preserved through extraction.
Place and station supply the surrounding location from which the household's social identity is detached.

structural_cues: The same فيها links 51:35-36, while plural المؤمنين is immediately answered by singular بيت and plural المسلمين.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: repeated فيها, plural extracted persons, and the sole بيت of submitters found afterward. Reader arrow: بيت denotes the household as a corporate enclave whose membership survives relocation. Alternative: بيت may be only the physical structure used to count occupants.

changed_reading.before: An unspecified number of individual believers are removed.
changed_reading.after: A household-scale enclave is extracted: plural believers remain one social house even as they are detached from the condemned place.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated فيها binds two opposite operations at one location: living occupants go out, while a visible trace is deliberately left in. Extraction therefore redistributes evidence rather than merely emptying the place.

activation_trace.role: Leaving an effect after departure supplies the retained residue that complements the removal of living occupants.
A manifest sign supplies the visible form taken by what remains inside after extraction.
Passage to the outside supplies the mobile side of the paired operation.
Disclosure from concealment lets removal and retained sign function together as a two-part revelation.

structural_cues: Consecutive first-person plural clauses repeat فيها: أخرجنا marks movement out, then تركنا ... آية marks deliberate retention within.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: extraction from فيها followed by leaving a visible sign in فيها. Reader arrow: these are complementary allocations of evidence, persons mobile and trace stationary. Alternative: the sign may memorialize only the punishment and bear no deliberate relation to the extracted persons.

changed_reading.before: The place is emptied of believers.
changed_reading.after: The scene is repartitioned: living believers are carried out while a visible trace is retained inside, so exit and residue jointly disclose the event.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers birth imagery from the preceding announcement to a civic rescue and relies on the form-distant birth branch of ق ر ب. It remains anchored in causative خروج from an interior and is reinforced by adjacent youth and barrenness branches; downstream prose should call it a birth-like material analogy, not a lexical meaning of أخرجنا.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: أخرجنا من كان فيها provides emergence from an enclosing interior, while the immediately preceding sequence juxtaposes approaching birth, youthful life, and a barren condition.

activation_trace.role: The approach of birth supplies the exploratory transition from enclosed life toward emergence.
Youthful new life supplies the viable issue brought across the imagined birth threshold.
Barrenness of womb and offspring supplies the closed, unproductive enclosure against which emergence is surprising.
Passage from an interior to the outside anchors the analogy in the focus's actual movement.
Place and emplacement supply the containing interior from which the faithful life is figuratively delivered.

changed_reading.before: The faithful occupants are evacuated from a doomed settlement.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the extraction resembles a birth: viable faithful life emerges from an enclosure otherwise framed by barrenness and closure.

strongest_changes: Entry and doubled peace turn the focus into the outward phase of a protected threshold reversal.
The commissioned, marked-target sequence changes rescue into complementary sorting and disclosure.
The sole-house audit and retained sign divide the aftermath between a mobile household and a stationary trace.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's roots support both physical exit and disclosure, and both security and assent; the context activates these pairs simultaneously while also sustaining a contained birth-like emergence analogy.
remaining_uncertainties: The safety resonance between سلام, المسلمين, and المؤمنين may be functional, or the terms may remain distinct identity labels.
The birth-like reading may overextend the form-distant ق ر ب branch despite its strong positional and enclosure anchors.
The retained sign may complement the extracted persons deliberately, or it may only record the judgment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Extraction operationalizes trusted assent as safety.** `خ ر ج/B002` supplies causing to come out; `ء م ن/B002` trusting assent and B001 settled security. Before marked harm falls, believers are removed from its field. I infer **assent/trust -> differentiated extraction -> security**. The verse makes faith a sorting relation with spatial consequence.
2. **Emergence from an enclosed place.** `خ ر ج/B001` is passage from within, the opposite of entering. This reverses the guests' entry in 51:25 and anticipates finding a single house in 51:36. I infer **enclosed threatened settlement -> protected persons brought outside**. The movement itself becomes rescue.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:55 later confirmed that belief remains a selective reception condition: here it differentiates rescue; there it differentiates benefit from reminder.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Protective extraction is the inverse movement of targeted impact.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `خ ر ج/B002` is “causing something to come out”; fixed `ك و ن/B001` supplies actual situated being; fixed `ء م ن/B001` is “settled security and trust,” with `B002` trusting assent. **Structural cue:** marked stones for limit-breakers precede (51:33–34), while the next ayah narrows what is found to one submitting house and 51:37 leaves a sign; Moses’ clear authority and Pharaoh’s seizure follow (51:38–40). **Role and abduction:** trust makes a protected relation, and causative exit relocates those in it before impact; I infer that marking and extraction are paired directions in one discriminating operation. **Reading change:** being brought out is not incidental evacuation but the positive, preserving side of the same sorting that sends consequence inward.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 51:36–40 confirmed the paired motions: one house remains as the preserved unit, while the later rejecter and his force are seized and cast in the opposite direction.

lexicalization_scope.note: Hem genel tasdik adlari hem de belirli soz obekleri ve dini kullanislar vardir; tanim bunlari yalin guven anlamina genisletmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir haber, vaat veya hakikati dogru sayip ona icten kabul ile yonelmektir. Dini kullanista bu kabul, kalp, dil ve davranisla baglanan bir boyun egme ya da seriate girme anlami kazanabilir.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek bir haberin, sozun veya hakikatin dogru sayilmasidir.
Hakka yonelik ic kabul, yalniz bilmekten ziyade boyun egme ve kabullenme bicimi alir.
Dini alanlarda bu kabul, bildirilen yola girme ve ona baglanma adi olarak kullanilir.
Ilahi sifat kullaniminda vaat edilen odulu dogrulama veya guvenceyle bildirme boyutu one cikar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dalin ortak cekirdegini tasdik olarak verir ve bir sozun dogru sayilmasini temsil eden ornegi buna baglar. Ayni iddia, daha ozel dini kullanimlarda hakka icten boyun egme, yola girme ve vaatle ilgili dogrulama boyutlarinin eklendigini de gosterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Haber, vaat, hakikat ve dini baglanma kullanimlarini tasdik cekirdegi etrafinda birlestirir.

error_profile.preserves: Dogru sayma, ic kabul ve daha ozel dini baglanma imkanini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Vaatle ilgili dogrulama tarafini korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel tasdik ve dini kabullenme alanlarini kapsamaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali dua icinde soylenen bir kabul istegi sozu ve bu sozu soyleme eylemi olarak verir. Cerceve, guven ve tasdik dallarindan ayrildigi ve sadece dua cevabi formuluyle ilgili oldugu icin uygundur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal guvenlik ya da tasdik degil; duada kabul talebini bildiren sabit sozdur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal belirli bir dua sozu ve onu soyleme eylemiyle sinirlidir; buradan genel guven ya da tasdik anlami cikarilmaz.

concept_map.definition: Dua sonunda kabul edilme istegini bildiren ve 'kabul et', 'oyle olsun' ya da 'bunu yap' anlaminda aciklanan sabit sozdur. Dal ayrica bu sozu soyleme eylemini ve kaynaklarda aktarılan ad yorumunu da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek, duada kabul istegini bildiren sabit cevap sozudur.
Kaynaklar sozun anlamini 'kabul et', 'oyle olsun' veya 'bunu yap' seklinde aciklar.
Bu sozu soyleme eylemi de ayni dal icinde adlandirilir.
Bazi aktarimlarda bu sozun ilahi bir ad oldugu yorumu da dalin yan rivayeti olarak bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ortak olarak dali dua icinde soylenen ve kabul istegi tasiyan sabit bir soz olarak anlatir. Ayni iddia, bu sozu soyleme eylemini ve sozun anlamina dair 'kabul et' ya da 'oyle olsun' aciklamalarini da icerir; ad yorumu ise bu ortak malzemenin yan aktarimidir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dua sonunda soylenen sabit kabul talebi ve onu soyleme eylemi icin genel karsiliktir.

error_profile.preserves: Dua baglamini, kabul istegini ve sabit soz niteligini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sozun dua icindeki anlamini eylemli bicimde cevirmek gerektiginde uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Sozun tek basina anlamini ve ad yorumu yanini kapsamaz.
